correctness.rationale: The volume and Q-Fano assertions are correct. At a vertex of Q_n, n independent coordinate bounds must be active. Two lower bounds are infeasible and n upper bounds force the remaining coordinate to be -2n; the complete vertex list thus has one coordinate i at -(2n-1), one free coordinate j at 1 and all others at 2. The list has n(n+1) primitive vertices; zero is interior. The negative polar is the anticanonical polytope, with normal fan the stated face fan (using the inward-normal convention). Independently of the proposed cap argument, the facet of the polar corresponding to (i,j) consists of -u_i/(2n-1) and u_k/2 for k distinct from i,j. Coning each such facet to zero gives a simplex of normalized volume 1/[(2n-1)2^(n-1)] because the unscaled vectors, up to one sign, are exactly the coordinate-function basis omitting u_j. Their interiors are disjoint and they exhaust the polar. This gives the formula, the three low-dimensional degrees, and asymptotic n/2^n, including n=2. The cap proof can also be justified: every pairwise barycentric sum is positive on the polar generators, so an edge from the single apex outside facet i intersects its supporting plane within that simplex facet.
residual_risks: The supplied numerical hull checker uses floating-point volume and tests dimensions 2–6 only. No part of the all-dimensional conclusion depends on it.

value.rationale: The family is naturally motivated by its small alpha invariant, and its exact degree can be a useful datum. But here the exact degree is already a routine determinant calculation from the published polar and facet data. The exponential decay is a direct restatement of that calculation, not a separate estimate or obstruction, and the record gives no distinct volume question that the calculation resolves. No genuine surviving non-routine claim is isolated by relabeling this family or by improving the cap proof.
residual_risks: No claim is made that anticanonical volumes or their use in future comparisons are generally unimportant.
